runner.text:
**Brief for the coach — Monday biceps change, recorded 4 Nov 2026**

**What I looked at**

I compared the previous system's two-week rotation with the program now in force. In the old plan direct biceps work was spread across the pull days: incline curls and hammer curls on Week A Saturday, dumbbell curls on Week A Sunday, incline curls on Week B Monday, dumbbell and hammer curls on Week B Sunday. In the current program, all direct biceps work sat in one session — Sunday's deadlift day: Bicep Curl (Dumbbell) 3 sets of 8–12 at RPE 8 and Hammer Curl (Dumbbell) 3 sets of 10–12 at RPE 8, six sets total. Monday (overhead press, chest-supported row, lateral raise, rear delt fly) had no curl, and was the lightest lifting day of the week. The program's per-muscle target is 10 hard sets a week; biceps also pick up indirect work from the rows, band pull-ups and negatives, plus the PT's chest-and-back Tuesday, which we estimate at 3 biceps sets every other week.

**The change**

Incline Curl (Dumbbell) added as the last exercise of Monday's session: 3 sets of 8–12 reps at RPE 8, 75 seconds rest, double progression — add load once every set reaches 12. Cues: bench about 45°, arms hang straight down behind the torso, elbows stay back with a full stretch at the bottom, no shoulder swing. This matches Joe's standing preference for dumbbell rather than barbell curls.

Reason recorded with the version: direct biceps work was six sets in one session; an incline curl on Monday makes it nine over two days, at long muscle length, and keeps the lightest lifting day inside its cap.

This is now the program in force — version 4, an amendment rather than a redesign. The current block, which opened 1 Nov 2026, continues unbroken; the rotation stays at week A. Nothing else changed: no session or exercise was removed or altered. Session time estimates after the change: Monday 53 minutes against its 75-minute cap; Wednesday 39 of 75; Friday 65 of 75; Saturday 65 of 90; Sunday 65 of 90. No start load was set for the incline curl — the first load will come from Joe's incline-curl history when the next week's plan is drafted; worth a glance then.

The targets, unchanged: bench 5 hard sets a week, overhead press 5, back squat 5, deadlift 4, pull-up 10 (counting negatives and band pull-ups). Deload rule: at most 6 hard weeks, then a week with sets cut 40%, loads unchanged, RPE capped at 8, and the priority lifts tested. Start loads on file: Farmers Walk 50 lb (recorded in Hevy as 45.36 kg), Kettlebell Swing 40 lb (18.14 kg) in both conditioning sessions.

**What has not happened yet — and what Joe must agree to**

Nothing in Hevy has changed. The program is recorded on our side only; the Monday routine in Joe's app still has four exercises. The incline curl reaches Hevy when the next week's plan is drafted and pushed, and that push is the one thing that needs his explicit approval. The Hevy check I ran alongside the change found nothing new between 20:40 and 20:53 on 4 Nov — no workouts, weigh-ins, routine or folder edits.

**Warnings — five, none blocking**

*Three routines in Hevy don't match the week plan approved on 2 Nov 2026.* Someone edited them in the app after the push. The differences: in one routine, the hold time on the second set of the first exercise; in another, the reps on sets 5, 6 and 7 of the first exercise and the weights on sets 1–3 of the second; in the third, the weights on sets 1–4 of the third exercise, the hold times on both sets of the fourth, and the weights on sets 1–3 of the sixth. The engine identifies them only by their Hevy reference, so I can't name the sessions with certainty from what came back. What it means: what Joe sees in the app for those sessions isn't exactly what the plan prescribed. What clears it: either the next week-plan push rewrites the routines back to the plan, or we record his edits as deliberate overrides on the next plan so they stick. Ask him whether those changes were intentional — that decides which way to go.

*Deadlift target of 4 sets is below the 5–15 band for a maintenance phase.* Left standing on coach judgement, carried over from the previous version: Sunday plans exactly four hard sets (one top set of 5 at RPE 8 and three back-off sets of 5), Friday's Romanian deadlift (3 sets of 6–10 at RPE 8) carries the hinge pattern, and the PT sometimes adds deadlifts on Tuesday. A target of 5 would flag under-target every week the session is done as written. It clears if a fifth hard deadlift set is added and the target raised to 5, or if the phase changes.

*The Friday strict pull-up test has no progression scheme, which doesn't fit a hypertrophy emphasis.* Left standing on coach judgement: 1 set of 1 rep at RPE 10 is the weekly measure while his max is one rep. The building happens through the negatives (Wednesday, 3 sets of 2–4) and band pull-ups (Wednesday 4 sets of 5–8, Sunday 3 sets of 5–8), each with its own progression. It clears when the test rep passes about five and the strict line is converted to real working sets.

**One more note**

The progress report has no dose history yet — the block opened 1 Nov, so there's no closed block to report on. First meaningful numbers come at the block boundary.

first.text:
Yes, it does. The hinge is covered twice a week with a heavy day and a moderate day, which is the shape you want for it.

**Hinge work in the current week**

| Day | Exercise | Hard sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sunday | Deadlift: one top set of 5 at RPE 8, three back-off sets of 5 | 4 |
| Friday | Romanian Deadlift: 3 sets of 6 to 10 at RPE 8 | 3 |
| Friday | Hip Thrust | glute-dominant, bridges the pattern |
| Conditioning days | Kettlebell swings | light, explosive hinge reps, optional |
| Tuesday | PT sometimes adds deadlifts | varies, not every week |

So the hamstrings and glutes get seven heavy hinge sets a week as a floor, spaced two days apart, plus the hip thrust and the split squat and Bulgarian split squat work for the glutes. The gap from Sunday's deadlifts to Friday's RDLs is five days and from Friday back to Sunday is two, which is enough recovery for either.

Why the deadlift itself stays at four: it is the most fatiguing lift in your week, Sunday also carries curls and pull-up work, and a heavy deadlift day piles on the lower back in a way RDLs do not. Four quality sets at RPE 8 is a sound weekly dose for a lift you are keeping strong rather than chasing. The Friday RDL does the volume work at lower spinal cost.

The one thing a hinge-heavy week does not give you is knee flexion: nothing in the program bends the knee against load the way a leg curl or nordic curl does. The old routine didn't have one either, so this is not a regression. I'd leave it for now. If after this block your hamstrings feel like the part of the lower body that isn't moving, a leg curl variant on Friday would be the first thing I'd add. The first real numbers on how each muscle has fared arrive when this block closes, so that is the natural moment to revisit it.
